To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the domains of Pauli-Fiezr type operators on arbitrary open subsets of the Euclidean space can be characterized by the corresponding Schrödinger operators, and that this characterization is stable under perturbations of the potentials by locally integrable functions.
the domains and operator core properties of Pauli-Fierze type operators are determined by those of the corresponding Diriclet-Schröinger operators and the quantized radiation field energy.

the domains of Dirichlet and Neumann realizations on Lipschitz or more general domains of Pauli-Fierze type operators are determined by those of the Dirichlet-Schroedinger operators, and that the operator cores of the Dirichiet realizations are determined by those cores and the cores of the radiation field energy operator, all in a natural way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of quantum systems consisting of matter particles and electromagnetic fields on general domains.
the mathematical foundations of quantum field models for non-relativistic particles interacting with quantized radiation fields in the presence of electromagnetic singularities.
the mathematical description of quantum systems consisting of matter particles confined to a bounded domain in space which are coupled to a quantized radiation field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the domain of the Neumann realization of a Pauli-Fierz operator is the closure of the domain of the Dirichlet realization with respect to the graph norm of the Dirichet-Schrödigner operator plus a certain quadratic form, and that the operator core of the Neumann Pauli-Fierz realization equals the operator core of its Dirichlet counterpart plus the operator core of this quadratic form.
the domain and the operator core of Pauli-Fierze type operators with singular potentials are determined by the domain and the core of the corresponding Schrödinger operator.
Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonians are essentially self-adjoint on the intersection of their natural domain with the operator core of the Dirichlet-Schödinger operators on the respective domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Dirichlet realization is always the smallest closed Pauli-Fierz-type operator with the given domain of the matter Hamiltonian and the given domain of a suitable radiation field energy, and the Neumann realization is the largest closed Pauli-Fierzt-type operator with the same domains.
the domain of a Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian is determined by the corresponding Schrödinger operator and the energy of the radiation field.
the domain and the operator core of a Pauli-Fierz-type operator are determined by the domain and operator core of the underlying Dirichlet-Schödinger operator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pauli-Fierz operators on general domains are much better behaved than their corresponding Schrödinger operators.
the domain and operator core properties of Pauli-Fiez type operators on general domains are essentially determined by those of Dirichlet-Schödinger operators, which are well-understood.
the domains of the Pauli-Fierz operator and its operator cores are independent of the choice of the electrostatic and magnetic potentials, provided that they satisfy certain conditions.
